svg.aria-label: Anatomy of one row: 68 bytes of page carrying a single bit of measurement, 0.18% payload. And the multiplication behind the row count: 365,133 sample points x 360 timesteps a day x 60 dates = 7,886,872,800 rows, which is also exactly 7,886,872,800 observations.
svg.text: One row, one bit — and where 7,886,872,800 of them come from
The table is fully normalised, so the row count IS the observation count. That identity is a property of this encoding, not an inevitability.
The v1 contract, and the whole of it — plus section_id and task_id, bookkeeping
The same row as bytes on the page
544 bits stored per row · 1 measured · 0.18% payload
At 7,886,872,800 rows that is ~499 GB of heap.
WHERE THE ROW COUNT COMES FROM
No array. No column per timestep. Nothing packed.
Let the bit's position carry the timestamp and the same 7.89 billion
observations fit in 2.2 GB — 225× smaller, and lossless. It is not
adopted because v1's three columns are the contract; DB_CLUSTER.md
